hypothesis: The newly preserved native stats OOB packet contains the same public profile as the lobby archive and can be validated and bound to the match client.
method: Default-off server --inspect-stats-upload assembles 1238-byte native chunks, requires exact zlib consumption and 32768-byte output, then reports only header metadata. It leaves statResponse unchanged, keeps no disk copy, and does not publish a profile when the CRC convention is unverified.
existing_source: Community native-engine codol_stats.c:93-123 defines Build 1649370 chunk:u8, wireLength:u16, 1238-byte parts and exact 32768-byte inflate.

Existing tools/ring_bridge_1649370.py:_fix_stats_payload explicitly records that the client upload header does not use the 2697 crc32(profile[4:]) convention and rewrites it only for a 2697 archive probe.

The local SQLite profiles table contains a 32764-byte public blob beginning with version 233 and schema 0x4a6cc345, and a 32764-byte secure blob beginning with version 19 and schema 0xa34378b4. This read-only comparison did not export either blob.

r836.first_probe: 32768-byte inflate succeeded but the initially over-strict 2697 CRC check returned profile_crc_mismatch; no profile published

interpretation: The transport and exact-size zlib decode are verified in independent runs, but the upload does not carry the expected public-profile header. Its role and CRC convention remain unknown. The 9-byte stats records in r837/r839 may be short control packets or still-truncated malformed packets and require a separate length audit. Neither a usable public profile nor an ESC loadout is established. Do not silently rewrite the upload CRC or bind this blob as player inventory.
cleanup: All experiment client, game-server and bridge processes ended or were stopped by verified exact PID. Only r107flow/runtime was used.
